entries.headline: Mijem Newcomm Tech launches up to $300,000 placement
entries.dek: The CSE-listed company's non-brokered offering carries three-year warrants that need shareholder approval before they can be issued.
entries.caption: Mijem Newcomm Tech Inc. has launched a non-brokered private placement of up to $300,000, expected to close on or about November 30.

sources.title: Mijem Announces Non-Brokered Private Placement of up to $300,000
Mijem Newcomm Tech Initiates Non-Brokered Private Placement to Raise $300,000

unverified_claims: The expected closing date of on or about November 30, 2026 is the company's own estimate and the offering may close in tranches on a different schedule.
Whether shareholder approval for the warrants will be obtained has not been determined; the release states only that unapproved warrants will be cancelled.
brief: Mijem Newcomm Tech Inc. (CSE: MJEM.X) said Oct. 19 it will offer up to 6,000,000 units in a non-brokered private placement at $0.05 per unit, for gross proceeds of up to $300,000. Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant.

The warrants are exercisable at $0.05 for 36 months following closing. Combined with the shares, the offering could result in the issuance of up to 12,000,000 common shares if the warrants are exercised in full. Closing is expected on or about November 30, 2026, and may occur in one or more tranches, subject to regulatory approvals including acceptance by the CSE.

Because the offering could result in the issuance of more than 100% of the company's outstanding securities, Mijem said it must obtain shareholder approval for the warrants at its next shareholder meeting; the warrants will be cancelled if that approval is not obtained. The company said net proceeds will be used for working capital.
body: Mijem Newcomm Tech Inc. (CSE: MJEM.X) said Oct. 19, 2026 that it will offer up to 6,000,000 units in a non-brokered private placement at $0.05 per unit, for gross proceeds of up to $300,000. Each unit comprises one common share and one common share purchase warrant.

The warrants are exercisable at $0.05 per share for 36 months following the closing date. Taken together with the shares in each unit, the offering could result in the issuance of up to 12,000,000 common shares on a fully diluted basis if all warrants are exercised. The release did not state the company's current number of shares outstanding.

The company said the offering is expected to close on or about November 30, 2026, and may close in one or more tranches, subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange.

Mijem said that because the offering could result in the issuance of more than 100% of its total outstanding securities, CSE Policy 4.6(2)(a) requires the company to obtain shareholder approval for the issuance of the warrants at its next shareholder meeting. If that approval is not obtained, the warrants will be cancelled.

All securities issued under the offering will be subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day after issuance, in accordance with Canadian securities law, the company said. It said net proceeds from the offering will be used for working capital.

The release did not describe Mijem's business, name any participating investors, or state whether any insiders are subscribing. It also gave no agent or finder, consistent with a non-brokered offering.

entries.headline: Canada's CPI rises 3.1% in September on energy prices
entries.dek: Statistics Canada said energy and gasoline prices drove the acceleration from August's 3.0% annual pace, even as food inflation eased to its slowest pace since mid-2024.
entries.caption: Statistics Canada reported the Consumer Price Index rose 3.1% year over year in September 2026, driven mainly by gasoline and energy prices.
brief: Statistics Canada said the Consumer Price Index rose 3.1% year over year in September, up from a 3.0% increase in August. On a monthly basis, the index rose 0.1% unadjusted, or 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis.

The agency said energy prices led the acceleration, with crude oil increasing in September to its highest level since May "amid ongoing uncertainty about the wars in the Middle East." Gasoline prices rose 27.8% year over year, up from 22.8% in August. Excluding gasoline, the CPI rose 2.2%, down from 2.4% the prior month.

Statistics Canada said food purchased from stores rose 1.7% year over year, the smallest increase since May 2024, while shelter costs rose 1.8%, up from 1.5% in August, which it tied to higher fuel oil costs and homeowners' insurance. The agency said five provinces saw faster price growth, mostly tied to gasoline and fuel oil costs.
body: Statistics Canada said the Consumer Price Index rose 3.1% year over year in September 2026, up from a 3.0% increase in August. On a monthly basis the index rose 0.1% on an unadjusted basis, or 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis.

The agency said energy prices led the September acceleration. It said crude oil prices increased during the month, reaching their highest level since May, "amid ongoing uncertainty about the wars in the Middle East." Gasoline prices rose 27.8% year over year in September, up from a 22.8% increase in August. Energy prices overall rose 19.0% year over year, compared with 15.4% in August.
Excluding gasoline, the CPI rose 2.2% year over year in September, down from 2.4% in August.

The agency said transportation costs, which include gasoline, rose 8.4% year over year in September. Prices for food purchased from stores rose 1.7% year over year, after increasing 2.8% in August, which it said was the smallest yearly increase in that category since May 2024.
Shelter prices rose 1.8% year over year in September, up from 1.5% in August, which the agency attributed to higher fuel oil costs and increases in homeowners' insurance.

Statistics Canada said five provinces experienced faster price growth in September, primarily due to elevated gasoline and fuel oil costs, and that Atlantic Canada showed notably higher inflation when energy costs were excluded from the regional comparison.

entries.headline: Gunnison Copper's ADRs set to trade on NYSE American
entries.dek: The Level II depositary receipt program begins trading October 26 under 'GUNN,' with no new shares issued and no capital raised through the listing.
entries.caption: Gunnison Copper's American Depositary Receipts are set to begin trading on the NYSE American under the ticker "GUNN" on October 26.

sources.title: Gunnison Copper to Commence Trading on NYSE American October 26, 2026, Under Ticker Symbol "GUNN"

unverified_claims: The preliminary economic assessment figures (NPV, IRR, payback period) are the company's own citation of a March 2026 technical report and have not been independently verified.
The stated resource tonnage and grade for the Gunnison Copper Project come from the company's own release and corresponding technical report.
brief: Gunnison Copper Corp. (TSX: GCU) said its American Depositary Receipts are expected to begin trading on the NYSE American under the ticker "GUNN" at the opening on or about Monday, October 26, 2026. Each ADR represents 30 common shares under a Level II ADR program, with The Bank of New York Mellon as depositary.

Starting October 23, 2026, U.S. shareholders may convert common shares into ADRs through BNY. The company said the program does not constitute a new offering of securities: no additional shares are being issued and no capital is being raised through the listing. Gunnison's shares continue trading on the TSX, OTCQB and Frankfurt Stock Exchange.

The listing remains subject to the effectiveness of the company's registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and final exchange approvals, Gunnison said. The release did not give a date by which that registration statement is expected to become effective.
body: Gunnison Copper Corp. (TSX: GCU, OTC: GCUMF, FSE: 3XS0) said its American Depositary Receipts are expected to commence trading on the NYSE American under the ticker symbol "GUNN" at the opening of trading on or about Monday, October 26, 2026. The listing is subject to the effectiveness of the company's registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and final exchange approvals, the company said.

Each ADR will represent thirty common shares of Gunnison, under a Level II ADR program with The Bank of New York Mellon acting as depositary bank. A Level II program allows a foreign company's existing shares to trade on a U.S. national exchange through depositary receipts, without the company raising new capital in the process.

Starting October 23, 2026, United States shareholders may convert their Gunnison common shares into ADRs through BNY. The company said explicitly that the ADR program does not constitute a new offering of securities, and that no additional common shares are being issued and no capital is being raised in connection with the NYSE American listing.

Gunnison's shares will continue to trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange, the OTCQB market and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange alongside the new U.S. listing. The release described Gunnison as a multi-asset copper developer and producer controlling the Cochise Mining District in Arizona.

The company's flagship Gunnison Copper Project carries a measured and indicated mineral resource in its main pit of more than 846 million tons at a copper grade of 0.33%, containing 5.19 billion pounds of copper, according to the release. A preliminary economic assessment completed in March 2026 for the project estimated an after-tax net present value, at an 8% discount rate, of $2 billion, an internal rate of return of 23% and a payback period of 3.9 years; full detail is in a technical report titled "Gunnison Project NI 43-101 Technical Report, Preliminary Economic Assessment, Cochise County, Arizona, USA," with an effective date of March 18, 2026, filed on SEDAR+.

Gunnison's Johnson Camp Mine is currently producing finished copper cathode through an on-site SX/EW facility, which the company said is fully funded by Nuton LLC, a Rio Tinto venture, with capacity of up to 25 million pounds of finished copper cathode annually. The release said Gunnison is supplying copper from that operation to the U.S. defense sector and to Amazon Web Services.
